title: Shared definitions of the Suderra edge contract

timestamp.description: UTC instant with second precision and a literal Z, e.g. 2026-10-20T12:00:00Z. Fractional seconds and offsets are not allowed, so TypeScript producers strip toISOString()'s .000.

digest.description: Digest set; contract 1.x defines sha256 only.

semver.description: Path-safe semantic version (DEC-1.10): it is used as a path component, so build metadata and empty identifiers are rejected.

os_version.description: OS version as published in /etc/os-release VERSION_ID: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, compared as an integer tuple (statements.json compatibility). Each component has at most 9 digits (at most 999999999), so every verifier, whatever its integer width, reads the same number.

fetch_url.description: A URL root fetches from on behalf of a signed statement (channels.json update_channel.fetch): https on port 443 (no port, or :443), a lowercase DNS name of at least two labels whose last label starts with a letter, so never an IP literal, no userinfo and no query or fragment. https_url is the wider form for the image's own cloud endpoint and the provisioning manifest, which a development image may point at an address and port.

board_profile.description: Board vocabulary; must equal the board_profile set of boards.json. x86 boards join as x86-ipc-<model> once a model is qualified (boards.json pending_board_families).

cargo_feature.description: Agent cargo features a Suderra OS release may carry in contract 1.x. tpm is absent on purpose: the agent gets no TPM device before the P2 TPM keystore (DEC-8 board matrix, DEC-21), so a release built with it would link tss2 and probe a TPM the unit never grants.

site_path.description: Site file path relative to /var/lib/suderra-site (= /data/suderra/site); fixed names, so no path component comes from a statement (DEC-1.10, DEC-4.2). io-config.yaml is the I/O map (tags, channels, alarm thresholds) in the format the agent persists for update_io_config on the generic channel (mutable-state.json ownership_notes).

base64.description: Canonical RFC 4648 standard base64 with padding (unused trailing bits zero).

ed25519_public_key.description: Canonical standard base64 of a raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key; its keyid is the SHA-256 of the 32 bytes.

device_binding.description: Hash of the OS-owned hardware identity (DEC-3.6): SHA-256 of the TPM EK public key, or SHA-256(BCM2711 serial || customer OTP value) on TPM-less RPi4/CM4, or SHA-256 of the DMI product_uuid on TPM-less x86 dev images only.

sequence.description: Monotonic per device and statement kind; root keeps the last accepted value in /data/suderra/os/seq/<kind> (DEC-2.4).

keyid.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key.

rauc_compatible.description: RAUC compatible string of an OS image: suderra-os-<board_profile> (boards.json rauc_compatible).

agent_abi_range.description: Inclusive agent ABI range MIN-MAX with decimal integers of at most 9 digits and MIN <= MAX, the syntax of SUDERRA_AGENT_ABI in /etc/os-release (statements.json compatibility). A range with MIN > MAX contains no ABI, so every installed agent lies outside it.

slug.description: Lowercase identifier: [a-z0-9] groups separated by single hyphens.

cidr4.description: IPv4 network in CIDR notation, dotted decimal without leading zeros. The host bits must be zero (10.0.0.0/24, never 10.0.0.5/24): checked by the verifier and reported as schema-invalid, because JSON Schema cannot state it. IPv6 is disabled on Suderra OS (sysctl), so no IPv6 form exists.

mac.description: Lowercase colon-separated MAC address of a network interface.

pci_path.description: Lowercase PCI address of a network interface as DDDD:BB:SS.F (sysfs form), stable across interface renames (DEC-11.6).

host.description: Lowercase fully qualified DNS name (RFC 1123 labels, at least one dot) or dotted-decimal IPv4 address, as a network peer is named in a signed site policy.

lifecycle_state.description: Root-owned lifecycle states (DEC-12); LOCKED is the fail-safe reading of an unknown, missing, corrupt or unmountable state.
